title: Present canonical Transaction type choices and scope-relative meaning

requirements.invariant: Canonical membership is the unordered Project set purchase/return/transfer and Business Inventory set purchase/return. Transfer is invalid in Business Inventory. Membership is not declaration, display, filter, default-selection or UI order.
LedgerTransactionType projects to exactly Purchase, Return or Transfer. Sale, Payment to Business, Fee, Expense, To Inventory, reimbursement, movement and legacy/import-review vocabulary are absent.

TransactionScopeOwnerKind.project projects to the exact owner title Client and businessInventory projects to 1584. Ownership is never inferred from names, identifiers, source strings, payer fields or storage location.

Presentation exposes TransactionClassification.economicMeaning unchanged: Purchase is scopeOwnerPaid, Return is scopeOwnerReceivedMoneyBack and Transfer is the one nonCashSameClientReallocation meaning. Transfer source and destination roles project identically; no incoming/outgoing, sign, debit/credit or budget direction is invented.

TransactionClassification remains the sole validated classification aggregate. Stateless presentation consumes it without recreating type/scope/role validity or economic meaning, persists no presentation value, and after canonical classification restart re-derives an identical descriptor without a port, query, operation, authorization or readiness contract.

Exactly two target-only Swift paths implement and test deterministic provider-free presentation while the Firebase application remains unchanged. No Firebase, Supabase, PowerSync, schema, app/MCP, migration, hosted-resource, release, cutover or production behavior advances.

items: TransactionTypeChoiceCatalog returns literal Set membership only: Project purchase/return/transfer and Business Inventory purchase/return. Set iteration and CaseIterable declaration order have no UI meaning.

TransactionTypeChoiceDescriptor contains only LedgerTransactionType, exact type title, TransactionScopeOwnerKind, exact scope-owner title and the existing TransactionEconomicMeaning. It has no public fieldwise initializer and no Codable conformance.

TransactionTypeChoicePresentationProjector accepts one already-valid TransactionClassification, reads its type, scope.ownerKind and economicMeaning, and deliberately omits role and identifiers so Transfer source/destination descriptors are equal.
No new failure type or alternate validity rules exist; invalid evidence is rejected by the verified TransactionTaxonomyFailure boundary before presentation.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: No Transaction, scope, presentation, membership, table, enum, constraint, index, view or migration is created or changed.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No Purchase, Return or Transfer command, eligibility, validation, write, correction or audit handler exists.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No relation, view or function is exposed through the Supabase Data API and no grant is added.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: A valid local classification or choice is not authorization. No membership, financial visibility or write RLS policy/test exists.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, local table, download predicate, upload connector, subscription or synchronized readiness contract exists.

items: Restart canonically encodes only the verified TransactionClassification and re-derives identical presentation after decode; presentation itself has no persisted or transient state.

The exact canonical encoder key allowlist remains classification type/scope/role and scope ownerKind/accountId plus projectId/clientId when present. Titles, meaning, order, amount, status, source and actions never serialize.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No receipt, AttachmentID, byte, URL, cache, upload, retention or deletion behavior exists.

appMcp.notApplicable: No SwiftUI menu, filter, layout, accessibility/order/default policy, MCP schema/tool/resource/handler or transport wiring is added.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No legacy Transaction value is decoded, classified, displayed or transformed. Sale, payment, fee, expense, reimbursement and movement evidence remain migration responsibilities.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: Existing bounded taxonomy failures are asserted as contract values only; no telemetry event, metric, alert, audit sink or runbook action is introduced.

items: Implementation remains inside provider-free LedgerTargetCore and its tests and does not change or link either application project.
The slice cannot choose or submit a Transaction, determine amount/sign/source/status/action, authorize a Principal, persist state, activate a feature, deploy, release or cut over.
O-002/O-011/O-012/O-013/O-014/O-015/O-028/O-029/O-030/O-031/O-032, A-003/A-004/A-015/A-016 and every provider/hosted/migration/production gate remain outside the boundary.

verification.expected: Set(LedgerTransactionType.allCases) equals the literal purchase/return/transfer set and allCases.count is exactly 3; literal Project catalog membership equals that set and literal Inventory membership equals purchase/return. Inventory excludes Transfer, and array/order equality is explicitly forbidden so declaration and Set iteration order cannot become UI policy.

All four standalone Project/Inventory Purchase/Return classifications project exact Purchase/Return, Client/1584 and the existing scopeOwnerPaid/scopeOwnerReceivedMoneyBack meanings using the canonical enum types rather than parallel presentation enums.

Valid project Transfer source and destination classifications with distinct scopes project equal descriptors containing only transfer/Transfer/project/Client/nonCashSameClientReallocation; role, Project identity, direction, amount sign and incoming/outgoing vocabulary are absent.

All six valid TransactionClassification shapes—Project and Inventory standalone Purchase/Return plus project transferSource and transferDestination—canonically encode/decode, emit only exact classification/scope key allowlists, preserve byte-identical canonical encoding and re-project identical non-Codable descriptors. Both restored Transfer descriptors are equal; no title, owner title, economic meaning, order or transient state serializes.

Unknown type/owner/role, malformed scope, incompatible role, Inventory Transfer, missing/wrong aggregate fields and malformed JSON fail through their exact existing TransactionTaxonomyFailure cases before presentation. Emitted display-title strings are exactly Purchase/Return/Transfer/Client/1584 and exclude all legacy/directional/amount/status/action terms.

A test-only consumer accepts each already-validated TransactionClassification and composes the catalog/projector without a second port, query or validity aggregate; all five valid owner/type pairs project canonically, both Transfer roles remain equivalent, and rejected taxonomy evidence yields no descriptor.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, provider/source-contamination and generated-contract checks, complete target tests, repeatable project generation, both staging builds and clean artifacts while only the two allowlisted target paths differ in the worker candidate.

notes: Ready only; no executable behavior yet. Independent scout and adversarial review narrowed this to literal unordered type membership and stateless presentation over the verified TransactionClassification. Actual-diff review then caught and corrected one P3: literal Set membership/count now explicitly forbids order equality, restart covers all six valid role-bearing classifications, and the exact-string assertion is limited to display titles. Final independent re-review found no remaining P0-P3 issue. The slice cannot recreate classification, claim UI/filter ordering, distinguish Transfer roles, classify legacy values, expose amounts/status/actions, or advance app/MCP, provider/schema/RLS/Sync, migration, hosted or production behavior.
